c Describe and explain the trends in electronegativity down the group and across a period in the periodic table. (Use correct terminology and include an explanation for electronegativity in your answer) (5 marks)
answerHtml:
Question 7

a i Ca

ii Ar

iii C or Si

iv Na

v O

(5 marks)

B Ionisation energy The energy required to remove one electron from an atom (1)

Ionisation energy decreases down a group (1) as the core charge stays the same, but the number of shells (or radius) increases so valence electrons are less attracted, therefore less energy required (1)

Ionisation energy increases across a period (1) as the core charge increases, but the number of shells is constant (or radius decreases) [1]

c. Electronegativity [5]

Electronegativity is the ability for an atom to attract electrons in a covalent bond towards itself (1)

Electronegativity decreases down a group (1) as the core charge stays the same, but the number of shells (or radius) increases so valence electrons are less attracted, therefore less energy required (1)

Electronegativity increases across a period (1) as the core charge increases, but the number of shells is constant (or radius decreases)
